title: Potato, roasted, fresh, peel not eaten, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Roasted potato is a whole tuber cooked in the oven without added fat. The peel is not consumed, leaving only the flesh and its natural nutrients. This cooking method preserves most of the vitamins and minerals found in fresh potatoes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 8,000 years.
Roasting brings out a natural sweetness through caramelization of sugars.
Without the peel, roasted potatoes are easier to digest for people with sensitive stomachs.
Roasted potatoes are often used as a base for healthy side dishes and diet meals.
Compared with fried potatoes, roasted potatoes contain far fewer calories and fat.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Fresh potatoes provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes roasted potatoes suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: If tubers are damaged or sprouting, solanine levels can rise; such parts should be removed.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Roasted potatoes can raise blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roasted potatoes are served as a side dish, diced into salads, used in casseroles, or enjoyed as a simple snack, seasoned with herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh potatoes in a cool, dark place at 4–10 °C. After roasting, let them cool, then keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
